clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work, then separated from Celeste; your mother lay awake over them; your brother Callum had ear infections all winter; and your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979, where her functioning came back. The shifts pass from one person to the next in these months, with no other change in the family marked among them.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest in pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984 through your sister Ines's birth in September: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and these shifts held together across the months as your mother's functioning could not support the household. Your sister Ines was born at the end of this period, where things settled into a new arrangement.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis in September 1986, across the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news; Hazel had a bad fall and her functioning declined; your uncle Lyle and your father argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; your father fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel; and your father drank most evenings. The shifts cluster through Hazel's moves into the nursing home in 1997, where your father cut his drinking back.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home for work, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's leaving home for a job up north in May 1999, within the following year: he and your father argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts move from your parents to your siblings in these months, settling as Ines's functioning came back.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following year: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going into the bookshop and lost that job; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; and by November you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then, so the period holds only your own trouble; what holds it together is that all your shifts fall in the months after her death and settle when you found new work.
